answer: Each identity posts a 40-credit bond for a work chain; outputs are hashed to a mirror ledger, and only a matching chain crosses the ledge to renewal. A summit panel re-audits 20 percent of chains. The kth identity sharing one wallet pays 50+20(k-1) credits, as the panel re-checks one extra prior chain per identity. For 1,000 fakes, bonds are 40,000 and surcharges 10,040,000. A rented-chain ring fails: mirror hashes bind each step to one key, so a rented step carries the renter key and mismatches at summit review, burning the bond. An honest agent pays one bond and one 50-credit surcharge.
